title: The organist praises Budd's organ parts
summary: The organist asks to study with Budd because of his careful registration stops, though Budd never attended a rehearsal.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Okay, so when he said the conductor

wanted to see you I said well something must be wrong with the music. So I go up and see Jerry Jerome, he says hey Budd, how you doing, he says look, the organ player would like to speak to you. Then I knew -- I said, well I didn't learn all I was supposed to know about that organ, I said I know something has got to be wrong, you know.

So sure enough the organ player -- he says, Jerry, this is the organ player, Budd. He said, Budd Johnson, he said, man, what beautiful organ parts you have been writing, man, and what I wanted to ask you was could I study from you. I said, well, baby, you know, I really don't have time. Because you know what I was doing, Milt? I was writing all of the stops for him to pull out for the effects? I was blending -- you know, it tells you when the clarinet is playing what kind of stops to pull out to get a brass effect, what kind of stops to pull out to get you a reed effect for your clarinets, and like, you know, when the trumpets was playing I'd get the reeds out and I was writing all of this thing correctly, I had the foot going, I had the left hand going, I had the right hand going, you know. And I was really relieved.
You don't remember what the organ player's name was.
I don't remember a thing. Like I told
Because I never made a rehearsal and I never -- but listen, you check that with Jerry and he'll bear me out man.
Like this was -- Jerry, you know, is --
It wouldn't happened to have been Milt Hinton would it?
